blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Self-attention-based vision backbones perform well on dense prediction, but the quadratic computational cost of global softmax attention limits their efficiency as image resolution increases. We introduce Gated Token Recurrence (GTR), a softmax-free recurrent vision backbone that combines gated linear attention, alternating spatial scan directions, and spatially enhanced SwiGLU blocks. GTR is distilled from a detection-specialized DINOv3 teacher using only final-layer patch-token alignment through a linear projection and squared ℓ 2 \ell_{2} loss, without masked-token prediction or intermediate-layer supervision. With Objects365 detector pre-training, GTR-L achieves 58.9 box AP on COCO val2017 with 1.908 ms median batch-one latency under compiled FP16 execution on an RTX 4090. The same backbone also transfers to instance segmentation, pose estimation, oriented detection, semantic segmentation, and monocular depth estimation. In an isolated kernel benchmark, our specialized chunkwise CUDA operator is 4.0 × 4.0\times faster than FLA v0.5.0 at 1.6K tokens on RTX 4090. TensorRT deployment on DRIVE AGX Thor achieves 2.282–8.769 ms median batch-one latency across the evaluated models. These results show that recurrent token mixing can provide an efficient alternative to global softmax attention for high-resolution dense prediction and edge deployment.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Self-attention-based vision backbones have shown strong performance for dense prediction ( Liu et al., 2026 ) . However, the quadratic complexity of softmax attention with respect to the number of image tokens makes high-resolution processing increasingly expensive, particularly on resource-constrained edge devices. Linear attention offers a promising alternative: EfficientViT ( Cai et al., 2023 ) demonstrates efficient on-device semantic segmentation, while ViG ( Liao et al., 2025 ) explores gated linear recurrence for detection and segmentation. Despite this progress, developing a general linear-attention backbone that performs consistently across diverse dense prediction tasks while meeting practical constraints on model size, computation, memory, and latency remains challenging. This motivates a central question: can linear attention support a general-purpose vision backbone that remains accurate across diverse dense prediction tasks while translating its theoretical efficiency into practical gains on edge hardware?
blocks.zh: 自觉视觉骨干显示强效致密预测(刘等,2026). 然而,在图像符号数量方面,软马克思注意力的四重复杂性使得高分辨率处理越来越昂贵,特别是在资源紧张的边缘设备上。 线性注意提供了一种有希望的替代办法:高效ViT(Cai等人,2023年)显示了高效的机载语义分解,而ViG(廖等人,2025年)则探索了有门线性重现,用于检测和分解. 尽管取得了这些进展,但发展一个总的线性关注主干线,在满足模型大小、计算、内存和耐久性的实际限制的同时,始终履行各种密集的预测任务,仍然是一项挑战。 这引发了一个中心问题:线性关注能否支持一个在各种密集预测任务中保持准确的通用视觉主干,同时将其理论效率转化为边缘硬件的实际收益?

blocks.en: We introduce Gated Token Recurrence (GTR) , a linear-complexity (in the number of image tokens) vision backbone designed to address this challenge. GTR builds on gated linear attention (GLA) ( Yang et al., 2024b ) with a softmax-free, single-scale recurrent architecture. It maintains a fixed patch grid across 12 blocks and performs one directional scan per block, cycling through four directions across depth to progressively aggregate global context. To complement this directional recurrence with explicit local spatial modeling, we introduce Spatial SwiGLU , which incorporates depthwise convolution into the value branch of SwiGLU ( Shazeer, 2020 ) to efficiently mix neighboring patches. Together, directional recurrence and Spatial SwiGLU provide complementary global and local spatial modeling while preserving linear complexity.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了Gated Token Recurrence(GTR),一种线性复杂性(在图像符号数量上)的视觉主干,旨在应对这一挑战. GTR基于有门的线性关注(GLA)(Yang et al., 2024b),具有柔软的无马克思,单级的重复建筑. 它维持一个跨越12个区块的固定补丁网格,每个区块进行一次方向扫描,通过4个纵深方向循环,逐渐汇总全球背景. 为了用明确的本地空间模型来补充这种定向重现,我们引入了Space SwiGLU(SwiGLU),它将深度折射纳入SwiGLU(Shazeer,2020年)的值分支,以高效地混合邻近的补丁. 定向重现和空间SwiGLU共同提供互补的全球和地方空间模型,同时保持线性复杂性。

blocks.en: Importantly, GTR uses a single distillation objective that supervises only the final patch tokens. Unlike ViT-Linearizer ( Wei and Chellappa, 2025 ) , which combines intermediate activation matching with masked prediction, or ViT-AdaLA ( Li et al., 2026b ) , which aligns attention modules before the final features, our approach distills only the final patch tokens. Specifically, GTR is aligned with a frozen, detection-specialized DINOv3 teacher ( Siméoni et al., 2025 ) using the same full-image input. A linear projection and a single squared ℓ 2 \ell_{2} loss constitute the entire distillation objective, requiring neither masking nor intermediate supervision.
blocks.zh: 重要的是,GTR使用单一的蒸馏目标,只监督最后的补丁符号. 不同于 ViT 学习器 (Wei和Chellappa,2025年),结合中间激活匹配蒙面预测,或VIT-AdaLA(Li等人,2026年b),在最终特征之前将注意力模块对齐,我们的方法只蒸馏最终的补丁符号. 具体来说,GTR与一个使用相同全图像输入的冷冻,检测专业的DINOv3教师(Siméoni等人,2025年)对齐. 线性投影和单平方 l 2\ell\2}损失构成整个蒸馏目标,既不需要遮掩,也不需要中间监督.

blocks.en: GTR scales across four model sizes (S, M, L, and X) and transfers to six dense prediction tasks: object detection, instance segmentation, human pose estimation, oriented object detection, semantic segmentation, and monocular depth estimation. With Objects365 detector pre-training ( Shao et al., 2019 ) , GTR-L achieves 58.9 box AP on COCO ( Lin et al., 2014 ) val2017 at a median forward-pass latency of only 1.908 ms under compiled FP16, batch-one inference on an RTX 4090. Beyond detection, GTR achieves competitive results in representative comparisons across the other five tasks using the same backbone design with task-specific heads and training recipes (Section 3.2 ; Appendix D ). As summarized in Figure 1 , GTR-S also exhibits slower growth in peak GPU memory and higher inference throughput than the softmax-attention-based EdgeCrafter-S ( Liu et al., 2026 ) as input resolution increases, highlighting the practical advantage of linear-complexity attention for high-resolution dense prediction.
blocks.zh: GTR尺度跨越4个模型大小(S,M,L,和X),并转移到6个密集的预测任务:物体检测,实例分解,人类姿势估计,定向物体检测,语义分解,以及单体深度估计. 通过Objects365探测器预训(Shao等人,2019年),GTR-L在COCO上实现58.9盒AP(Lin等人,2014年) val 2017,在编译的FP16中位数前传空位仅为1.908 ms,批次一推论为RTX 4090. 除了检测外,GTR在使用相同的主干设计和特定任务负责人和培训配方(第3.2节;附录D)对另外五个任务进行具有代表性的比较时取得了竞争性的结果。 如图1所汇总,GTR-S在输入分辨率增加时,也表现出GPU峰值内存增长较慢,推论吞吐量比基于软马克思的EdgeCrafter-S(刘等人,2026年)要高分辨率密度预测的线性-复杂性关注的实际优势.

blocks.en: Finally, we bridge architectural efficiency and real-world deployment with dedicated system optimizations. We develop a specialized chunkwise CUDA operator for GLA ( Yang et al., 2024b ) that computes chunk summaries in parallel while propagating recurrent context through a boundary-state scan. The operator achieves a 4.0 × 4.0\times speedup over FLA v0.5.0 ( Yang and Zhang, 2024 ) at 1.6K tokens under FP16 and CUDA Graph execution on an RTX 4090. For end-to-end deployment on DRIVE AGX Thor, we further integrate fused kernels and graph transformations into TensorRT ( NVIDIA, 2026 ) . Across six tasks and four model scales, GTR achieves median FP16 batch-one latencies of 2.282–8.769 ms, demonstrating its practicality for real-time dense prediction on edge hardware.
blocks.zh: 最后,我们将建筑效率和现实世界的部署与专门的系统优化联系起来。 我们为GLA(Yang等人,2024年b)开发了专门的分块式CUDA操作器,通过边界状态扫描来平行计算分块摘要,同时传播反复出现的情况。 运营商在FP16和CUDA Graph执行的RTX 4090下,以1.6K的符号在FLA v0.5.0(Yang and Zhang, 2024)上实现4.0×4.0\时速加速. 对于DRIVE AGX Thor的端到端部署,我们进一步将引信内核和图变集成TensorRT(NVIDIA,2026). 通过6项任务和4个模型尺度,GTR实现了FP16批1的中位数2.282–8.769 ms的延迟,显示了其在边缘硬件上实时密集预测的实用性.

blocks.en: In summary, our main contributions are: • We introduce GTR , a single-scale, linear-attention vision backbone for efficient dense prediction. GTR combines gated token recurrence with four-directional scanning across depth and Spatial SwiGLU for complementary global and local spatial modeling. • We demonstrate the generality and scalability of GTR across six dense prediction tasks and four model scales. The same backbone design transfers effectively across object-level and pixel-level tasks using simple final-token distillation and task-specific adaptation. • We enable practical edge deployment through a specialized chunkwise CUDA operator and TensorRT integration. Across six tasks and four model scales, GTR achieves low-latency FP16 inference on DRIVE AGX Thor, demonstrating low-latency deployment on automotive edge hardware.
blocks.zh: 总而言之,我们的主要贡献是: 我们引入了GTR, 一个单一尺度,线性视线主干 高效的密集预测。 GTR将门形符号重现与跨深度的四向扫描和Space SwiGLU相结合,以补充全球和地方空间模型。 我们通过6个密集的预测任务和4个模型尺度,展示了全球资源变化评估的通用性和可扩展性。 相同的主干设计在对象级和像素级任务之间有效转移,使用简单的最终托盘蒸馏和任务特定改造. ^ 我们通过一个专门分块的CUDA操作员和TensorRT集成使实际边缘部署成为可能。 通过6项任务和4个模型尺度,GTR实现了对DRIVE AGX Thor的低纬度FP16推论,显示了在汽车边缘硬件上的低纬度部署.

blocks.en: 2 Method
blocks.zh: 2 方法

blocks.en: Figure 2 provides an overview of GTR and its object detection pipeline. We first describe the GTR backbone, followed by its distillation strategy and specialized chunkwise inference. Given an image 𝐈 ∈ ℝ H × W × 3 \mathbf{I}\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times 3} , GTR produces a stride-16 grid of L = H ​ W / 16 2 L=HW/16^{2} patch tokens and maintains the same resolution throughout 12 blocks. Each block combines gated linear attention (GLA) ( Yang et al., 2024b ) for long-range context with Spatial SwiGLU for local spatial mixing. The scan direction cycles through four directions across successive blocks to aggregate context from different orientations. For object detection, features from blocks 4, 8, and 12 are used to build a lightweight feature pyramid at strides 8, 16, and 32, followed by a DETR-style decoder ( Carion et al., 2020 ; Peng et al., 2025 ) . The GTR backbone itself remains single-scale, while multi-scale features are constructed in the detection neck. Details of the neck and decoder are provided in Appendix B , and the four GTR model configurations in Appendix D.1.1 .

blocks.en: Since the recurrence is causal along its scan order, a single scan captures context from only one direction. To model two-dimensional context, GTR cycles through four scan directions across successive blocks (see Figure 2 ): left-to-right, right-to-left, top-to-bottom, and bottom-to-top. Each block performs only one directional scan and restores the original spatial order afterward. Across depth, the alternating directions allow tokens to progressively receive complementary spatial context.

blocks.en: The chunkwise formulation of GLA ( Yang et al., 2024b ) rewrites the token-wise recurrence as efficient matrix operations within fixed-size chunks. Our implementation follows a simple three-stage procedure: we first compute chunk summaries in parallel, then propagate context across chunk boundaries through a lightweight recurrent scan, and finally compute the outputs of all chunks independently. Our inference-only operator is specialized for the GTR configuration: FP16 inputs, chunk size C = 64 C=64 , per-head dimensions d k = 32 d_{k}=32 and d v = 64 d_{v}=64 , and a zero initial state. Training continues to use the reference FLA kernels ( Yang and Zhang, 2024 ) . The operator takes the same queries, keys, values, and learned log-decays 𝒈 t = log ⁡ 𝜸 t \bm{g}_{t}=\log\bm{\gamma}_{t} as the original recurrence.

blocks.en: 3 Experiments
blocks.zh: 3 个实验

blocks.en: In this section, we evaluate GTR across diverse dense prediction tasks and analyze its key design choices. We first evaluate GTR on object detection, and then transfer the backbone to five additional tasks: instance segmentation, human pose estimation, oriented object detection, semantic segmentation, and monocular depth estimation. Each task uses a task-specific head, initialization, and training recipe, as detailed in Appendix D . The main paper focuses on recent competitive methods, with more comprehensive comparisons provided in Appendix C . We conclude with ablations of the main architectural and training choices.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们评价各种密集预测任务的GTR并分析其关键设计选择. 我们首先对物体检测进行GTR评价,然后将骨干转移到另外五个任务上:实例分解,人类姿势估计,定向对象检测,语义分解,以及单体深度估计. 如附录D所详述的,每项任务均使用具体任务负责人、初始化和培训配方。 主要文件侧重于最近的竞争方法,附录C提供了更全面的比较。 在结束发言时,我们详细介绍了主要的建筑和培训选择。

After backbone distillation, the main GTR detectors are trained for 36 epochs on Objects365 ( Shao et al., 2019 ) , followed by 30 epochs on COCO ( Lin et al., 2014 ) train2017 . For latency, we benchmark all models on an RTX 4090 using FP16, batch size one, torch.compile , and CUDA Graphs, and report median CUDA-event latency after warm-up. We measure the network forward pass for DETR-style models and additionally include CUDA NMS for methods that require separate post-processing. Baseline accuracy is taken from the corresponding sources, while latency is measured under our setup.
Full training and latency protocols are provided in Appendices D and E.2 , respectively.

blocks.en: We ablate the main design choices of GTR, including the distillation objective, spatial modeling, token mixer, input resolution, and detector pre-training. All detection results are evaluated on COCO ( Lin et al., 2014 ) val2017 . For architectural ablations, each variant is independently distilled using the same teacher and image pool, followed by the same downstream training schedule. Full settings and results are provided in Appendix C.7 .

For ViT-Linearizer, we use the best mask ratio (0.5) from a sweep over 0.2–0.9. Despite its simple single-stage design and objective, our method achieves 50.7 AP, outperforming ViT-Linearizer (50.0) and ViT-AdaLA (48.2), while training from scratch reaches only 31.1 AP. This suggests that simple final-output alignment is effective for distilling GTR.

Replacing GLA with softmax attention in three of the twelve backbone blocks yields similar accuracy (55.4–55.6 vs. 55.5 AP), but increases median latency from 1.908 to 2.094–2.117 ms and computation from 106 to 119 GFLOPs. blocks.en: High-performance linear-attention kernels are typically designed for LLMs on server GPUs using Python/Triton stacks ( Qwen Team, 2026 ; Team et al., 2025 ) , whereas automotive deployment requires efficient execution within a production inference engine. We deploy GTR on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor with TensorRT ( NVIDIA, 2026 ) through graph–kernel co-optimization: standard TensorRT operators are combined with fused CUDA kernels for GLA and S-SwiGLU to reduce kernel launches and global-memory traffic without changing the computation. This enables low-latency inference across all six dense-prediction tasks, while maintaining at least 0.9989 0.9989 cosine similarity to the PyTorch FP32 reference across all 48 task–scale–batch configurations. Appendix E.1 provides platform details, Roofline analysis ( Williams et al., 2009 ) , and complete latency results.
blocks.zh: 高性能线性内核一般是使用Python/Triton堆栈(Quen Team,2026;Team等人,2025年)为服务器GPU上的LLMs设计的,而汽车部署则需要在生产推论引擎内高效执行. 我们在NVIDIA DRAVE AGX Thor上部署GTR,与TensorRT(NVIDIA,2026)通过图-内核协同优化:标准Tensor RT运营商与GLA和S-SwiGLU的已引信的CUDA内核结合,在不改变计算的情况下减少内核发射和全球-分子流量. 这样可以对所有6个密集预测任务进行低纬度推论,同时在所有48个任务-规模-批量配置中保持至少0.9989 0.9989 余弦与PyTorch FP32参考的相似性。 附录E.1提供了平台细节,Roofline分析(Williams等人,2009年),以及完整的延迟结果.

blocks.en: 4 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 4 结论

blocks.en: We presented GTR, an efficient softmax-free backbone for dense prediction. GTR combines a homogeneous GLA architecture with simple final-output distillation and optimized inference execution. Across object detection and five additional dense-prediction tasks, GTR achieves a strong accuracy–efficiency trade-off, while deployment on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor demonstrates its practicality on automotive hardware. These results show that linear attention can serve as an effective and efficient alternative to softmax attention for dense visual prediction.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了GTR, 一个高效的无软马克思的骨干 用于密集的预测。 GTR将一个单一的GLA架构与简单的最终输出蒸馏和优化推论执行结合起来. 通过物体探测和另外五项密集预测任务,GTR实现了强精度-效率权衡,而NVIDIA DRAVE AGX Thor的部署则显示了其在汽车硬件上的实用性。 这些结果显示,线性注意力可以作为一种有效而高效的替代软马克思注意力来进行密集的视觉预测.

Linear attention factorizes kernelized attention and exploits associativity to
avoid materializing the dense token-to-token matrix, reducing complexity from O ⁡ ( L 2 ) O(L^{2}) to O ⁡ ( L ) O(L) and admitting recurrent
evaluation ( Katharopoulos et al., 2020 ) . Modern linear-time recurrent
families, including RetNet ( Sun et al., 2023 ) , RWKV ( Peng et al., 2023a ) , Mamba ( Gu and Dao, 2024 ) , DeltaNet ( Yang et al., 2024c ) , and GLA ( Yang et al., 2024b ) , enrich the recurrent
state with retention, selectivity, delta-rule updates, or data-dependent gates
while retaining parallel or chunkwise training
forms.
ViG ( Liao et al., 2025 ) is the closest architectural precedent: it adapts GLA to vision with within-block bidirectional modeling, direction-wise gating, and local two-dimensional interaction, and provides non-hierarchical and hierarchical variants. Its fused bidirectional kernel also targets practical efficiency. GTR uses one scan per block, alternates directions across depth, and introduces local mixing in the SwiGLU channel mixer. We evaluate these choices together with a detection-specialized distillation recipe and task-specific deployment.

blocks.en: Hybrid approaches such as MambaVision ( Hatamizadeh and Kautz, 2025 ) and SoLA-Vision ( Li et al., 2026a ) combine recurrent or linear mixers with softmax attention. Our hybrid ablation tests three softmax-layer placements within GTR-L. Kernel-based vision alternatives include LaplacianFormer’s low-rank Laplacian attention ( Feng et al., 2026 ) . blocks.en:

For each target stride s ∈ { 8 , 16 , 32 } s\in\{8,16,32\} , we first align all selected features to the same spatial resolution: 𝐗 ~ l ( s ) = ℛ s ​ ( 𝐗 l ) , l ∈ { 4 , 8 , 12 } , \widetilde{\mathbf{X}}_{l}^{(s)}=\mathcal{R}_{s}(\mathbf{X}_{l}),\quad l\in\{4,8,12\}, (5) where ℛ s ​ ( ⋅ ) \mathcal{R}_{s}(\cdot) resizes each feature map to the target stride s ∈ { 8 , 16 , 32 } s\in\{8,16,32\} using bilinear interpolation; no resampling is applied when the source and
target strides are identical.
For each target scale, the aligned features from different semantic depths are concatenated along the channel dimension and fused by a lightweight C2f module ( Jocher, 2023 ) : 𝐏 ( s ) = C2f s ​ ( Concat ⁡ [ 𝐗 ~ 4 ( s ) , 𝐗 ~ 8 ( s ) , 𝐗 ~ 12 ( s ) ] ) , s ∈ { 8 , 16 , 32 } . \mathbf{P}^{(s)}=\mathrm{C2f}_{s}\left(\mathrm{Concat}[\widetilde{\mathbf{X}}_{4}^{(s)},\widetilde{\mathbf{X}}_{8}^{(s)},\widetilde{\mathbf{X}}_{12}^{(s)}]\right),\quad s\in\{8,16,32\}. channel dimensions.
Compared with heavier feature-pyramid encoders, this design keeps the encoder compact while aggregating early, middle, and late backbone representations at every detection scale.

multi-scale memory for the decoder.

In Virtual KITTI 2, sky pixels are encoded with a depth of 655.35 m; we clip these values to 80 m while retaining them as valid. For DIODE and SUN RGB-D, depth values are clipped to 80 m and 10 m, respectively. Across all datasets, training and evaluation use a common maximum depth of 100 m, with depths in the range [ 10 − 3 , 100 ] [10^{-3},100] m considered valid.

The default DA3 inference pipeline assumes multi-view inputs from a common
scene rather than a batch of independent images: it couples the views in a
batch through cross-view attention, shared scale alignment, and joint
percentile-based depth normalization. Batching unrelated ImageNet images
therefore makes each prediction depend on the other images in the batch; we
measured median relative deviations of 68 68 – 233 % 233\% from single-image
inference. To batch efficiently while preserving single-image behavior, we feed
each sample as a single-view input, yielding tensors of shape ( B , 1 , 3 , H , W ) (B,1,3,H,W) ,
and run global alignment and post-processing independently for each batch
element. The resulting predictions match single-image inference to within 0.1 % 0.1\% relative error. We further bucket images by their resolution after
teacher preprocessing rather than by their original resolution, so that every
batch shares a single resolution while images with common aspect ratios can
still be grouped together. Overall, batching with resolution bucketing reduces
the number of teacher forward passes by a factor of approximately 8 8 .

The measured-depth datasets differ by more than an order of magnitude in size,
ranging from roughly 10K images in SUN RGB-D to over 300K in TartanAir. To
mitigate this imbalance, we oversample each dataset with an integer repetition
factor, using [ 6 , 3 , 2 , 2 , 2 , 1 , 3 ] [6,3,2,2,2,1,3] in data-loader order. The pseudo-labeled ImageNet pool is drawn from a separate

random square cropping. Composition-based geometric augmentations such as
Mosaic, ZoomOut, and IoUCrop are disabled, since they alter the relationship
between image scale and metric depth and thus break geometric consistency.

For DOTA-v1.0, we follow the multi-scale training and testing protocol of
RiO-DETR ( Hu et al., 2026 ) : during both training and testing, each image is
rescaled by factors of { 0.5 , 1.0 , 1.5 } \{0.5,1.0,1.5\} and then cropped into 1024 × 1024 1024\times 1024 patches with a
stride of 524 524 pixels, i.e., an overlap of 500 500 pixels. The task-specific
OBB decoder consists of four layers and introduces three modifications for
oriented object detection. First, we adopt angle distribution
refinement (ADR) ( Ding et al., 2026 ) , which represents each oriented box
by six discrete distributions: four distances to the sides of its
axis-aligned enclosing box and two vertex offsets. These distributions are
decoded into oriented boxes by a distance-to-rotated-box conversion, which
avoids the angular boundary discontinuity of direct angle regression.
Second, we rotate the sampling offsets of deformable attention by the
predicted angle θ \theta of each query, so that the sampling pattern aligns
with the principal direction of the target. Third, oriented contrastive
denoising (OCD) ( Ding et al., 2026 ) perturbs only the axis-aligned
coordinates ( x 1 , y 1 , x 2 , y 2 ) (x_{1},y_{1},x_{2},y_{2}) of the denoising queries and leaves the
angle channel unchanged.

blocks.en: Figure 13 visualizes reconstructions obtained from all 49 calibrated views of each DTU object. Since a single image does not geometrically determine absolute depth scale, depth maps predicted independently across views may exhibit view-dependent scale drift. Prior to fusion, we therefore align the scale of each predicted depth map using a single scalar, computed as the median ratio between the projected structured-light reference depth and the prediction over valid pixels. This per-view rescaling preserves the relative depth structure within each view while correcting only its global scale.

blocks.en: We then back-project the rescaled depth maps using the calibrated camera intrinsics and extrinsics, fuse all 49 views into a TSDF ( Curless and Levoy, 1996 ) volume with 2-mm voxels, and render the resulting surface as colored points. blocks.en: To visualize multi-frame geometric consistency, for each reference time t t , we aggregate all available frames within [ t − 4 ​ s , t + 4 ​ s ] [t-4\,\mathrm{s},\,t+4\,\mathrm{s}] . For each frame, we scale-align the GTR-L depth prediction using a single scalar estimated from the corresponding LiDAR measurements, back-project the corrected depth with the camera intrinsics, and transform the resulting points into a common coordinate frame using the calibrated pose. We then fuse all observations with TSDF ( Curless and Levoy, 1996 ) to obtain a local map. Figures 17 and 18 show two examples from perspective and bird’s-eye views. Since LiDAR is used only for per-frame scale alignment, these results qualitatively illustrate geometric consistency after scale correction.
blocks.zh: 为可视化多帧几何一致性,每个参考时间 t t,我们汇总所有在 [t - 4 s, t + 4 s] [t-4\,\mathrm{s},\,t+4\,\mathrm{s} 范围内可用的帧. 对于每个帧,我们使用从相应的LiDAR测量中估计的单面标尺对GTR-L深度预测进行比例调整,用相机内在的图像对校正深度进行反投射,并利用校准的姿势将产生的点转换成共同坐标框架. 然后,我们用TSDF(Curless and Levoy,1996年)将所有观测数据进行整合,以获得本地地图。 图17和图18从视角和鸟眼角度说明了两个例子。 由于LiDAR只用于每帧比例尺对齐,这些结果在质量上说明了比例尺修正后的几何一致性.
